$comment: Illustrative config for a pnpm + turbo monorepo (an Electron-style desktop app, a web app, shared packages) — copy this file to your repo root as repo-gates.config.json and adjust the package names/paths. Anything omitted falls back to DEFAULT_CONFIG (see the README's Reference table). Unlike the README's jsonc snippet, this file is strict JSON — no // comments — since repo-gates.config.json itself is parsed strictly; use nested "$comment" keys for notes instead, as below.

coverage.$comment: check-coverage holds each package to its OWN floor (gates/coverage-budgets.json) — a well-covered package can't mask a thin one. `repo-gates check-coverage --init` seeds the floors from your current tree.

bundleSize.$comment: Each target is built via `turbo run build --filter <filter>` (cached), then dist is measured per bucket and ratcheted (raw + gzip totals, largest single chunk). `check-bundle-size --init` re-baselines.

agents.$comment: check-agents fails if a `pnpm run <script>` or backticked path in these docs no longer resolves — keeps agent-facing docs honest as the repo changes.

report.$comment: Non-gating dashboard (report-test-timing) rendered into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY — reads each package's junit output.

$boundaries_comment: Architectural import rules -> ESLint, via @kellykampen/repo-gates/eslint-boundaries (see README 'Import boundaries'). ESLint flat config is last-wins per rule, so each file scope is ONE boundary carrying ALL its pattern groups; nested scopes re-include the broader patterns via `extends` instead of copy-paste.

patterns.message: Apps must not import each other — share code through packages/*.
Renderer is a browser context — reach main via IPC, not a value import (import type is fine).
